text:
alex wang: Heads-up — customer acme-inc hit a 429 on project `acme-frontend` yesterday even though the quota dashboard showed ~1.2M tokens remaining for that project. Their invoice shows ~1.9M tokens billed for the month. They want an explanation and possible credit. Repro steps in thread.
maya patel: thanks. do we have request_ids/times for the 429s? which deployment/region? cc @rui chen for metering.
alex wang: yes, sample from their support attachment:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk-debug-....
Project-Id: acme-frontend
Timestamp: 2025-11-07T18:32:12Z

Response: 429 Too Many Requests
Headers:
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000000
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  X-RateLimit-Reset: 169* (unix)
  X-Request-Id: req_01Fxxxx
  X-Org-Id: org_acme
```
They also included a sample of their dashboard screenshot showing 1,200,000 tokens remaining at 2025-11-07T18:30Z (attached). Invoice lines for the org show 1,900,000 tokens for Nov so far.
rui chen: initial hypothesis: meter pipeline may be emitting records to both project and org aggregations (fanout) due to the recent org-aggregation change. If the dashboard is showing a per-project remaining value but billing aggregator is summing org-level events differently, you can see a disparity.
Attempted quick checks:
- splunk query I ran: `index=metering event_type=token_emit project_id="acme-frontend" | stats sum(tokens) by ingestion_time_window`
- noticed duplicate emits with same `request_id` but different `aggregation_target` (project + org) for a subset of events between 18:20-18:40 UTC.
samir khan: for billing: invoices are computed from billing-aggregator which consumes the post-processed (deduped) topic. If dedupe keys differ from the real-time dashboard pipeline, counts can diverge. We need start/end intervals and affected request_ids to estimate credit.
alex wang: here's a minimal repro script the customer used that reliably produced 429s in ~10-20 requests using their production token (scrubbed below). They ran it from us-east-1:
```
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-XXX" \
    -H "Project-Id: acme-frontend" \
    -d '{"input":"test token count"}' \
    -D - | sed -n '1,20p'
  sleep 1
done
```
maya patel: @alex can you drop the exact list of problematic `X-Request-Id` and the screenshot urls into the ticket? I'll ask customer to confirm sample timeframe and give permission for a billing review.
devex-bot: New ticket created: SUP-8742 - "acme-inc: apparent quota mismatch and 429s" (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-8742)
oncall-bot: paging rui chen for support (pager duty)
rui chen: I dug further. Root cause appears to be a regression in the metering fanout logic introduced in PR #1421 (deployed 2025-11-06 03:12 UTC). When `emit_on_org` flag is true and `project_tag` exists, the pipeline created two events with the same tokens but different `aggregation_key` (one keyed by project_id, one keyed by org_id). The real-time dashboard deduplicates by `project_id` (so shows remaining correctly for project), but the billing path aggregated both events for org-level billing due to a missing dedupe key, doubling some tokens for the invoice window.
Proof snippet from the raw producer logs (redacted):
```
{"request_id":"req_01Fxxxx","project_id":"acme-frontend","org_id":"org_acme","tokens":120,
 "aggregation_target":"project","emit_time":"2025-11-07T18:32:12.123Z"}
{"request_id":"req_01Fxxxx","project_id":"acme-frontend","org_id":"org_acme","tokens":120,
 "aggregation_target":"org","emit_time":"2025-11-07T18:32:12.124Z"}
```
alex wang: confirmed — I pulled the logs the customer sent and attached 7 matching `request_id`s that show the double emit pattern.
samir khan: thanks. For credits: we estimate duplicated tokens ~190k for the org between 2025-11-01 and 2025-11-07. I'll need the final list of affected request_ids + projects to produce precise credit numbers. We can issue an interim credit while we finish the audit.
maya patel: action items:
  1) @rui to push hotfix to meter pipeline to stop double emits and add an idempotence key (ingest_id) — target +2h.
  2) @rui to deploy metric that reports `dashboard_count - billing_count` per-org for rolling windows (15m/1h) so we can alert if divergence > 5%.
  3) @samir to compute provisional credit and prepare billing adjustment for acme-inc (need request_ids + estimate window).
  4) @alex to coordinate with customer and attach the list and grant permission for billing work.
rui chen: working on PR now. Quick mitigation: toggle the feature flag `org_agg_fanout_enabled=false` in staging/prod to stop the extra emit path while fix lands. I'll also add a dedupe on `request_id` at the billing-aggregator consumer as a safety net.
alex wang: I've asked acme support contact to confirm and gave them the SUP-8742 link. They agreed to provide the request_id list and gave permission for a billing audit.
samir khan: once I have the request_ids I can run a mapreduce on the billing topic and produce an exact duplicate-token sum. Then we can draft the credit note.
maya patel: thanks team. Please post PR/FF toggles and the time you flip them. Customer expects at least a short-term fix by EOD UTC- they are queue-blocked.
rui chen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/1429 . I toggled `org_agg_fanout_enabled=false` in prod at 2025-11-07T20:05:00Z — monitoring now. I'll post follow-up in ~30m with metrics.
oncall-bot: incident note recorded SUP-8742 - mitigation toggled by rui chen at 2025-11-07T20:05:00Z
alex wang: customer confirmed rate limits stopped happening after 20:10Z (they did a small smoke test). They asked if we can proactively reconcile the over-count on the invoice.
samir khan: proceeding with provisional credit calc. ETA for final numbers: 24h after I receive request_ids.
maya patel: closing loop with customer now and will keep ticket open until credit is applied + billing reconciliation is posted.
rui chen: will follow up with a postmortem draft in `#postmortems` once billing numbers are finalized. Preliminary root cause: meter fanout + missing dedupe in billing path.
